message:
My array headroom covers the milk-bottle hold for Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Plain words: the pinch to hold a heavy jar squeezes well below where the taxels bottom out, so grip force and light touch fit together. I take up the required normal per finger calculation (E85) from Dr. Elena Vasquez which states 9.81 N per finger to hold 1.00 kg at friction 0.500, and from micro-transduction that spreads to 125 kPa in the pressure at 9.81 N hold (E93), inside 213 kPa at 50 N in the dual-range strain sweep 1mN to 50N grip without saturation (E64), about a firm thumb press and therefore everyday pinch.

Friction gives further margin for Dr. Amara Okafor.

Plain words: tacky silicone grips better than the slippery case assumed, so real hold needs even less squeeze than the worst case above. I take up the Bar Mat Vs Silicone Grip Liner (E88) from Dr. Amara Okafor which states dry silicone grip near 0.880, which from micro-transduction means the 0.500 friction in the required normal per finger calculation (E85) is conservative and the 125 kPa in the pressure at 9.81 N hold (E93) is an upper bound, still inside the dual-range sweep (E64).

Ready, because 125 kPa hold sits mid-range with 14.6 Least Significant Bit, where Least Significant Bit means LSB, steps at 1 mN and faceted drape keeps crosstalk flat, leaving only the named timed-loop bench test with Dr. Elena Vasquez and Dr. Marcus Reid.
